items.title: Fernandes: Man Utd have offered new deal but now is not time for talks
items.excerpt: Bruno Fernandes exclusively told Sky Sports that Manchester United have offered him a new contract but he has put discussions on hold as he insists the club's priority must be returning to winning ways.
body: Bruno Fernandes exclusively told Sky Sports that Manchester United have offered him a new contract but he has put discussions on hold as he insists the club's priority must be returning to winning ways.

Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United , Sky Sports News understands, with his current deal due to expire at the end of the season. The club's initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began over a new deal, but was turned down by the Portuguese, who signed his last contract in August 2024.

United hold an option to extend the 32-year-old's stay at Old Trafford by a further year, which would also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January over the possibility of a free transfer. items.title: De Zerbi compares Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal - who is Spurs teen?
items.excerpt: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.
body: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.

De Zerbi turned to the highly rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half.

After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months, and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich.

items.title: How 'complacent' Arsenal unravelled at Newcastle - and their key lesson
items.excerpt: From "exceptional" to "complacent" - Arsenal's drop-off in the second half at Newcastle was extraordinary.
body: From "exceptional" to "complacent" - Arsenal's drop-off in the second half at Newcastle was extraordinary.

Noni Madueke's equaliser at least rescued a point, but after completely dominating the first half at St James' Park Mikel Arteta says his team have learnt a harsh lesson about the need to deliver a complete performance in the Premier League.

Credit has to go to Newcastle, who were energised by Matthias Jaissle's triple substitution at half-time, with Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga bringing intensity. Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw brought the goals. But the Premier League champions were their own worst enemy and, in the end, were fortunate to get away with their lead at the top of the table improved - for now.

With Man City dropping points again on Saturday and surprise-package Brighton still to play on Sunday, Arsenal remain firmly in the box seat. But Arteta is eager to drive even higher standards in his squad this season as he builds on last year's success - and he was far from impressed with how his team allowed Newcastle back into the game.

items.title: Hearts put eight goals past 10-man Dundee in thumping win
items.excerpt: Hearts returned to winning ways in spectacular style as they destroyed 10-man Dundee 8-0 at Dens.
body: Hearts returned to winning ways in spectacular style as they destroyed 10-man Dundee 8-0 at Dens.

The Jam Tarts went into the game on the back of a run of three straight defeats but they ran riot against the Dark Blues, netting four in the first half thanks to Sabah Kerjota, a Pierre Landry Kabore double and an own goal by Ryan Finnigan.

Dundee were reduced to 10 men after the break with Owen Bevan shown a straight red card before Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Kerjota with his second and Stuart Findlay blew Dundee away with four more goals.
